newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates steady to softer amid good avai.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates steady to softer amid good avai.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates in most regions were steady to softer with relaxed demand restricted to modern tonnage keeping competition for business strong, brokers said.
The combination of growing tonnage avails, particularly that of older tonnage, with modern vessels now getting much of the work at cheaper levels, continues to cap any upside for rates.

However, some of the more busier routes saw slight improvements of 1-2 points in worldscale assessments, noteably cross Mediterranean and Caribbean upcoast trips where business for 80,000 and 70,000 tonne quick turnaround voyages has been moderately active, traders said.

Mideast Gulf/Red Sea trade to eastern destinations continued active, although thinner today, to hold rates for VLCCs steady with voyages to Japan holding around W56-7 and S.Korea and Red Sea routes taking an unchanged W52-53.
Rates to the West valued W50 for USG and W52.5 for UK-Cont.

West Africa rates for Suezmax tonnage remained soft, slipping 1-1/2 points to trade at W91 to the U.S. Atlantic coast. Brokers said there was ample tonnage available with spill-over tonnage from quieter Med markets looking for business. Bookings to Spain were also weaker easing around five points to W97.5 for mid-Nov voyage.
Inter UK/Cont rates also eased around 2-1/2 points to value around W107.5 in thin activity with Aframax tonnage continuing to get the bulk of the work.
Cross Med activity continued to give Aframax tonnage reasonable employment and rates here improved slightly with Ras Lanuf to Trieste taking a steady W105.
Surplus tonnage and thin demand capped rates for Suezmax tonnage at around W85.
In the Western hemisphere moderate Caribs upcoast trade pushed rates for 70,000 tonne cargoes up a couple of points to around W132.5. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
